Cumulative Probability Table for a Discrete Distribution

Source: R/numerical_fallbacks.R
disc_cum_table.Rd

Builds the cumulative pmf from the support lower bound, growing the table geometrically until it covers the probability and the support point asked for.

Usage

disc_cum_table(distrib, theta, need_p = -Inf, need_k = -Inf, kmax = 1e+06)

Arguments

distrib

An object inheriting from class "discrete_distrib".

theta

A named list of parameters.

need_p

Grow the table until it covers at least this probability.

need_k

Grow the table until it reaches at least this support point.

kmax

A ceiling on the table size, to bound a runaway request.

Value

A list holding the support points and their cumulative probabilities.

Details

This is the whole of the discrete fallback: the cdf, the quantile function and the random generator are all lookups into it. No new algorithm was needed for discrete distributions, because the cdf of a discrete variable is a step function and inverting it is exact. The cost was one R-level call per draw, and the lookup is vectorized.

Requires a finite lower bound, which every standard count distribution has.
